section: Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi - Kubja Vishnuvardhana, dynastic history, patronage of Telugu (Nannaya)
subsections: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: The Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi were originally a branch of which dynasty?
accepted.x: The Eastern Chalukyas were founded as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas after Pulakeshin II conquered the Vengi region.
accepted.tq: Identify the parent dynasty before considering closely related Chalukya branches.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Who appointed Kubja Vishnuvardhana as the viceroy of Vengi?
accepted.x: Pulakeshin II conquered Vengi and appointed his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as its viceroy.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–relative–office relationship to avoid swapping the Chalukya rulers.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared his independence and founded the Eastern Chalukya line in:
accepted.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana became viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.
accepted.tq: Separate the appointment year from the later year of independence.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
accepted.x: The boar, or Varaha, was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among dynastic emblems rather than titles or capitals.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Pulakeshin II conquered the Krishna–Godavari region.
2. Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
3. Sanskrit was their official language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Pulakeshin II conquered the Krishna–Godavari region, Kubja Vishnuvardhana was his brother, and Sanskrit was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which ruler is associated with the title “Yuvaraja” in the Kopparam plates?
accepted.x: The Kopparam plates refer to Kubja Vishnuvardhana by the title “Yuvaraja.”
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with the ruler named in it.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
accepted.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
accepted.tq: Use the temple–builder pair rather than confusing it with later Vengi temples.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: The title “Samastha Bhuvanashraya” was borne by:
accepted.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I bore the title “Samastha Bhuvanashraya.”
accepted.tq: Match the exact royal title with its ruler.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contribution of Vishnuvardhana III?
o: He founded the Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu.
He gave Mushikonda village to the Jains.
He defeated Satyasraya with Chola assistance.
accepted.x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.
accepted.tq: Avoid the ruler–achievement swap by linking the grant to Vishnuvardhana III.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Kokkili, who briefly occupied the Eastern Chalukya throne, subsequently established the kingdom of:
accepted.x: Vishnuvardhana III recovered the throne from Kokkili, who then established the Yalamanchili kingdom.
accepted.tq: Trace the consequence of a succession dispute instead of confusing a kingdom with a capital.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Vijayaditya II is associated with which of the following claims?
accepted.x: Vijayaditya II is described as having fought 108 battles; he is also associated with the construction of 108 Shiva temples.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar numerical traditions attached to different Eastern Chalukya rulers.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s:
With reference to Chalukya Bhima I, consider the following statements:
1. He is credited with 360 battles in the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva.
2. He ruled for 30 years.
3. He built the Pancharamas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are associated with Chalukya Bhima I: the 360 battles, a 30-year reign and the construction of the Pancharamas.
accepted.tq: Combine the numerical, duration and architectural clues belonging to one ruler.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which inscription records that Chalukya Bhima I fought 360 battles?
accepted.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva records the tradition of Chalukya Bhima I fighting 360 battles.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with the specific numerical information it records.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, the commander of:
accepted.x: Panduranga, the commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription.
accepted.tq: Identify the subordinate–ruler relationship instead of attributing the inscription directly to a king.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Tripura Martya Maheshwara was the title of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, not Amma I. Saktivarman I, Rajaraja Narendra and Vimaladitya are correctly matched as shown.
accepted.tq: Find the single title–ruler mismatch among otherwise familiar pairs.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Saktivarman I regained the Vengi throne with the help of Rajaraja Chola and defeated the army of:
accepted.x: Saktivarman I, with Rajaraja Chola’s assistance, defeated the Kalyani army led by Satyasraya in 1006.
accepted.tq: Match the political ally and opponent in the Chalukya–Chola conflict.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: The discovery of Eastern Chalukya coins in Arakan is associated with:
accepted.x: Coins of Saktivarman I have been found in Arakan, present-day Burma.
accepted.tq: Link the ruler to the geographical evidence associated with his coinage.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Vimaladitya strengthened the Chola connection of the Eastern Chalukyas by marrying:
o: Ayyana Mahadevi, daughter of Pulakeshin II
Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
accepted.x: Vimaladitya married Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja Chola I.
accepted.tq: Use the marriage alliance to distinguish Vimaladitya from other Eastern Chalukya rulers.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned on:
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned on 16 August 1022.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact day, month and year rather than only the approximate reign period.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was associated with Rajaraja Narendra?
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra bore the title “Kavyageetha Priyudu”; Rajarajanarayana and Baraganda Bhairava were also associated with him.
accepted.tq: Separate the titles of Rajaraja Narendra from those of earlier rulers.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared independence
B. Saktivarman I defeated Satyasraya
C. Rajaraja Narendra was crowned
D. Vijayaditya VII was ousted by Rajendra Chalukya
accepted.x: The events occurred in 624 CE, 1006 CE, 1022 CE and 1070 CE respectively.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Vijayaditya VII, the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukyas, was ousted in 1070 CE by:
o: Rajendra Chalukya, later known as Kulottunga I
accepted.x: Rajendra Chalukya ousted Vijayaditya VII in 1070 CE and later became known as Kulottunga I.
accepted.tq: Identify the successor’s alternate name to avoid a person–title confusion.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Who seized Vengi after killing Danarnava during the interlude in Eastern Chalukya history?
accepted.x: The Telugu Choda ruler Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and seized Vengi until Danarnava’s sons recovered it with Chola assistance.
accepted.tq: Track the succession interruption through the killer and the displaced ruler.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: The Kopparam inscription of Pulakeshin II refers to present-day Mangalagiri as:
accepted.x: The Kopparam inscription calls Mangalagiri “Mangalapura.”
accepted.tq: Match the historical place-name with its present-day identification.
accepted.sec: Ruler → title + contribution (Kubja Vishnuvardhana to Rajaraja Narendra)

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the architectural style associated with the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: A purely Buddhist style without a Dravidian element
A monolithic rock-cut style derived exclusively from Jain architecture
A Vesara or Chalukya style blending a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence
A purely Nagara style with no local features
accepted.x: The Eastern Chalukya style is described as Vesara or Chalukya style, combining a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence.
accepted.tq: Use the defining architectural features to eliminate absolute descriptions such as “purely” and “exclusively.”
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Vengi school of temple architecture?
o: Buddhist style, brick stupas and a wooden vimana
Vesara style, granite domes and a circular jagati
Dravida style, local sandstone and a raised jagati
Nagara style, marble construction and an underground sanctum
accepted.x: The Vengi school is described as Dravida in style, using local sandstone and a raised jagati.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete architectural combination rather than one isolated feature.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
accepted.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure temple group and match it to its builder.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: The Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu and the Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry are associated with:
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra is associated with both the Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu and the Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry.
accepted.tq: Pair two monuments with their common patron to avoid a builder swap.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: Why were the three Shiva temples at Kalidindi constructed according to the tradition associated with Rajaraja Narendra?
o: They marked the conquest of the Vishnukundins.
They were built for Jain monks from Mushikonda.
They served as royal coronation temples.
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra constructed the three Shiva temples at Kalidindi in memory of fallen Chola soldiers.
accepted.tq: Connect the monument with its stated commemorative purpose.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot are attributed to:
accepted.x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Bhimeswara temples from the separate 108-temple tradition.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: Which temple contains carved figures of the Ganga and Yamuna?
accepted.x: The Vijayeshwara temple is noted for its carved figures of the river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive sculptural detail to identify the temple.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
accepted.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
accepted.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.
accepted.sec: Temples → ruler + style (108 Saiva temples, Pancharamas, Draksharama, Biccavolu)
